hypotheses: A morphism f:Sh(C)→Sh(D) and eleven precisely enumerated properties of its right adjoint f_* and counit f^-1f_*.
conclusions: Implications (a)–(h) in the statement, including (3)⇔(9), (4)⇔(11), and (2)⇔(7), and all of their one-way consequences.

hypotheses: A morphism of sites f:D→C from a continuous u:C→D, with the property that any D-cover of u(U) is dominated, as a map of associated representable sheaves, by images of a C-cover of U.
conclusions: The direct-image functor f_* preserves surjective morphisms of sheaves.

hypotheses: A morphism of sites f:D→C represented by u:C→D, and every V in D is covered by objects of the form u(U_i).
conclusions: f_* reflects injections and surjections of sheaves.

hypotheses: A site C and object U.
conclusions: Sheaf-theoretic emptiness, the singleton-section property for all sheaves, nonemptiness or singleton value of the sheafification of the empty presheaf, and existence of the empty covering of U are equivalent.
Sheaf-theoretic emptiness is inherited by every object mapping to U.

hypotheses: Continuous and almost cocontinuous u:C→D, and presheaf G on D singleton-valued on all sheaf-theoretically empty objects.
conclusions: (u^pG)# equals u^p(G#).

hypotheses: A continuous and almost cocontinuous u:C→D between sites.
conclusions: u^s=u^p on sheaves preserves pushouts, coequalizers, and finite connected colimits.

hypotheses: A site morphism f:D→C from continuous u:C→D, where u is also almost cocontinuous.
conclusions: The direct image f_* preserves pushouts, coequalizers, and finite connected colimits.

hypotheses: A site C and a sheaf F.
conclusions: F is a subterminal object if and only if the localized topos Sh(C)/F embeds as a subtopos of Sh(C).

hypotheses: A site C and subterminal sheaf F.
conclusions: The full subcategory of G with F×G→F an isomorphism forms a subtopos.

hypotheses: A closed immersion of topoi i:Sh(D)→Sh(C).
conclusions: i_* is fully faithful; preserves surjections, coequalizers and pushouts; reflects injections, surjections and bijections.

hypotheses: A continuous u:C→D with C having final X mapped to a final object of D and with C fibre products preserved by u; this gives the site morphism f:D→C.
conclusions: The adjoint pullback/pushforward pair extends to sheaves (and presheaves) of algebraic structures, and commutes with the underlying set-valued sheaf (or presheaf).

hypotheses: A site C, parallel arrows a,b:V→U whose associated representable sheaves coequalize to the final sheaf.
conclusions: Global sections Γ(C,F) identify with the equalizer of a*,b*:F(U)⇒F(V).

hypotheses: A category C and object U.
conclusions: Sieves on U form a set, ordered by inclusion.
Unions, intersections and smallest generated sieves exist; the maximal sieve is h_U and the minimal sieve empty.

hypotheses: A category C, object U, sieve S and arrow f:V→U belonging to S.
conclusions: The pullback sieve S×_U V is maximal, i.e. h_V.

hypotheses: A Grothendieck topology J on C and object U.
conclusions: J(U) is closed under finite intersections and upward inclusion of sieves.

hypotheses: A set-indexed family of topologies J_i on one category C.
conclusions: Their pointwise intersection defines a topology.
There exists a coarsest topology finer than every J_i.

hypotheses: A collection of presheaves F_i on C and the sieves S whose restrictions remain bijective after every pullback V→U.
conclusions: This assignment J of sieves is a Grothendieck topology, and is the finest topology for which every F_i is a sheaf.

hypotheses: A site C; define J(U) as those sieves containing one generated by a covering family in the site.
conclusions: J defines a Grothendieck topology on C.
A presheaf is a sheaf for J exactly when it is a sheaf for the original covering families of C.

hypotheses: A category C with Grothendieck topology J, and presheaf F of sets, using the covering-sieve colimit construction L.
conclusions: LF is separated.
If F is separated, LF is a sheaf and F→LF is injective.
If F is a sheaf, F→LF is an isomorphism.
L(LF) is always a sheaf.

hypotheses: A category C with Grothendieck topology J, a presheaf F and a sheaf G.
conclusions: Every map F→G factors uniquely through sheafification F→F# as a sheaf morphism F#→G.

hypotheses: A category C with topology J, an object U, and sieve S⊂h_U.
conclusions: S is a covering sieve if and only if its sheafification S#→h_U# is an isomorphism.

hypotheses: A category C and two Grothendieck topologies J and J'.
conclusions: J=J' if and only if the categories of sheaves for J and J' coincide.

hypotheses: A category C and two topologies J,J' on it.
conclusions: J⊂J' if and only if every sheaf for the finer topology J' is a sheaf for J.
